title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 63 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 434–435 (Night 63, continuing directly from nights-62), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 63 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān, still on the chapter on good manners (adab), tells how ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb called his treasurer Muʿayqib to account for a single dirham, and how ʿUthmān's son helped himself to a dirham of the revenue; then, on the report of Aslam, how ʿUmar carried flour and fat on his own back to a hungry woman and her children and cooked for them. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-sittūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixty-third night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ قَالَتْ وَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مُعَيْقِبٌ عَامِلًا عَلَى بَيْتِ الْمَالِ فِي خِلَافَةِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Nuzhata al-Zamāni qālat wa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu kāna Muʿayqibun ʿāmilan ʿalā bayti al-māli fī khilāfati ʿUmara ibni al-Khaṭṭābi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate, that Nuzhat al-Zamān said: And know, O king, that Muʿayqib was a worker over the house of the wealth in the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nuzhat al-Zamān said: And know, O king, that Muʿayqib was the officer in charge of the public treasury in the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and أن together as one word (السَّعِيدُأَنَّ); it is kept as printed. Last night's sentence is repeated here, because that night broke off just as the anecdote was about to begin.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ رَأَى ابْنَ عُمَرَ فَأَعْطَاهُ دِرْهَمًا مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa annahu raʾā ibna ʿUmara fa-aʿṭāhu dirhaman min bayti al-māli
sentences.l: And it so-happened that he saw the son of ʿUmar, and gave him a dirham from the house of the wealth.
sentences.i: It happened that he met ʿUmar's son and gave him a dirham from the public treasury.
sentences.n: ابْن عُمَر is ʿUmar's son (the tradition names him ʿAbd Allāh); the print does not. Throughout, "he" in the first sentences is Muʿayqib, who then takes up the tale in his own voice.

sentences.t: قَالَ مُعَيْقِبٌ وَبَعْدَ أَنْ أَعْطَيْتُهُ الدِّرْهَمَ انْصَرَفْتُ إِلَى بَيْتِي فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا جَالِسٌ وَإِذَا رَسُولُ عُمَرَ جَاءَنِي فَرَهِبْتُ مِنْهُ وَتَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَإِذَا الدِّرْهَمُ فِي يَدِهِ
sentences.tr: qāla Muʿayqibun wa-baʿda an aʿṭaytuhu al-dirhama inṣaraftu ilā baytī fa-baynamā anā jālisun wa-idhā rasūlu ʿUmara jāʾanī fa-rahibtu minhu wa-tawajjahtu ilayhi fa-idhā al-dirhamu fī yadihi
sentences.l: Muʿayqib said: And after that I gave him the dirham, I went away to my house; and while I was sitting, and behold, the messenger of ʿUmar had come to me; and I was afraid of him and turned toward him, and behold, the dirham was in his hand.
sentences.i: Muʿayqib said: After I had given him the dirham I went home. While I was sitting there, a messenger from ʿUmar came to me. I was afraid of him and went to him, and there was the dirham in his hand.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا after فَبَيْنَمَا ("while…") is the usual way of marking what suddenly appears; the main verb comes after it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَيْحَكَ يَا مُعَيْقِبُ إِنِّي وَجَدْتُ فِي نَفْسِكَ شَيْأً قُلْتُ وَمَا ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī waylaka yā Muʿayqibu innī wajadtu fī nafsika shayʾan qultu wa-mā dhālika
sentences.l: And he said to me: Woe-to-you, O Muʿayqib, I have found in your self something. I said: And what is that?
sentences.i: He said to me: Woe to you, Muʿayqib! I have found something in your heart. I said: And what is that?
sentences.n: وَيْحَك is a mild exclamation of reproach, "alas for you", not a curse. The print spells شيئًا as شيأ, with the hamza written on the alif; it is pointed here as شَيْأً.

sentences.t: قَالَ إِنَّكَ تُخَاصِمُ أُمَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي هَذَا الدِّرْهَمِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla innaka tukhāṣimu ummata Muḥammadin ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama fī hādhā al-dirhami yawma al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: He said: Truly you will contend with the nation of Muḥammad, God bless him and give him peace, over this dirham, on the day of the standing.
sentences.i: He said: On the Day of Resurrection you will be disputing with the community of Muḥammad, God bless him and give him peace, over this dirham.
sentences.n: The point of the rebuke: a dirham of the public treasury belongs to the whole community, so giving it away unasked will have to be answered for on the Day of Resurrection. The present tense تُخَاصِمُ here looks ahead.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبَ عُمَرُ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ كِتَابًا مَضْمُونُهُ إِذَا جَاءَكَ كِتَابِي هَذَا فَأَعْطِ النَّاسَ الَّذِي لَهُمْ وَاحْمِلْ إِلَيَّ مَا بَقِيَ فَفَعَلَ
sentences.tr: wa-kataba ʿUmaru ilā Abī Mūsā al-Ashʿariyyi kitāban maḍmūnuhu idhā jāʾaka kitābī hādhā fa-aʿṭi al-nāsa alladhī lahum wa-iḥmil ilayya mā baqiya fa-faʿala
sentences.l: And ʿUmar wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī a letter, its contents: When this letter of mine comes to you, give the people that which is theirs, and carry to me what remains. And he did so.
sentences.i: And ʿUmar wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī a letter to this effect: When this letter of mine reaches you, pay the people what is due to them and send me whatever is left. And he did so.
sentences.n: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī was ʿUmar's governor (of Basra and then Kufa). The letter is the lesson of the anecdote: pay what is owed from the revenue first, and send only the remainder to the caliph.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَلِيَ عُثْمَانُ الْخِلَافَةَ كَتَبَ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَفَعَلَ وَجَاءَ زِيَادٌ مَعَهُ فَلَمَّا وَضَعَ الْخَرَاجَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عُثْمَانَ جَاءَ وَلَدُهُ فَأَخَذَ مِنْهُ دِرْهَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waliya ʿUthmānu al-khilāfata kataba ilā Abī Mūsā mithla dhālika fa-faʿala wa-jāʾa Ziyādun maʿahu fa-lammā waḍaʿa al-kharāja bayna yadayi ʿUthmāna jāʾa waladuhu fa-akhadha minhu dirhaman
sentences.l: And when ʿUthmān took-charge of the caliphate, he wrote to Abū Mūsā the like of that, and he did so; and Ziyād came with him. And when he put the tribute between the two hands of ʿUthmān, his child came and took from it a dirham.
sentences.i: When ʿUthmān became caliph he wrote the same to Abū Mūsā, who did so, and Ziyād came with him. When the revenue was laid before ʿUthmān, ʿUthmān's son came and took a dirham from it.
sentences.n: The print does not say who Ziyād is beyond his coming with Abū Mūsā. بَيْنَ يَدَيْ "between the two hands of" means "in front of, in the presence of". وَلَدُهُ "his child" is taken as ʿUthmān's son, as the next lines show.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى زِيَادٌ فَقَالَ عُثْمَانُ مَا يُبْكِيكَ قَالَ أَتَيْتُ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ فَأَخَذَ ابْنُهُ دِرْهَمًا فَأَمَرَ بِنَزْعِهِ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَابْنُكَ أَخَذَ فَلَمْ أَرَ أَحَدًا قَالَ لَهُ شَيْأً أَوْ يَنْزِعُهُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā Ziyādun fa-qāla ʿUthmānu mā yubkīka qāla ataytu ʿUmara ibna al-Khaṭṭābi bi-mithli dhālika fa-akhadha ibnuhu dirhaman fa-amara bi-nazʿihi min yadihi wa-ibnuka akhadha fa-lam ara aḥadan qāla lahu shayʾan aw yanziʿuhu minhu
sentences.l: And Ziyād wept; and ʿUthmān said: What makes you weep? He said: I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb with the like of that, and his son took a dirham, and he ordered its removal from his hand; and your son took, and I did not see anyone who said to him anything or who removes it from him.
sentences.i: Ziyād wept, and ʿUthmān said: What makes you weep? He said: I brought ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb the like of this, and his son took a dirham, and ʿUmar ordered it taken out of his hand. Your son has taken one, and I have seen no one tell him a thing or take it from him.
sentences.n: The last clause is loosely built in the print (قَالَ … أَوْ يَنْزِعُهُ, "who said … or who removes"); the sense is that no one in ʿUthmān's court reproved the son or took the dirham back.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عُثْمَانُ وَأَيْنَ تَلْقَى مِثْلَ عُمَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿUthmānu wa-ayna talqā mithla ʿUmara
sentences.l: And ʿUthmān said: And where do you find the like of ʿUmar?
sentences.i: ʿUthmān said: And where would you find the like of ʿUmar?

sentences.t: وَرَوَى زَيْدُ بْنُ أَسْلَمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ خَرَجْتُ مَعَ عُمَرَ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ حَتَّى أَشْرَفْنَا عَلَى نَارٍ تُضْرَمُ
sentences.tr: wa-rawā Zaydu bnu Aslama ʿan abīhi annahu qāla kharajtu maʿa ʿUmara dhāta laylatin ḥattā ashrafnā ʿalā nārin tuḍramu
sentences.l: And Zayd ibn Aslam related from his father that he said: I went out with ʿUmar one night, until we overlooked a fire being kindled.
sentences.i: And Zayd ibn Aslam related, from his father, that he said: I went out with ʿUmar one night until we came in sight of a fire that was being kindled.
sentences.n: Zayd ibn Aslam, a scholar of Medina, reports from his father Aslam, ʿUmar's freedman and companion, who speaks from here on. ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ "one night" is an adverbial accusative.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَسْلَمُ إِنِّي أَحْسِبُ هَؤُلَاءِ رَكْبًا أَضَّرَبِهِمُ الْبَرْدُ فَانْطَلِقْ بِنَا إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Aslamu innī aḥsibu hāʾulāʾi rakban aḍarra bihimu al-bardu fa-inṭaliq binā ilayhim
sentences.l: And he said: O Aslam, I reckon these a party-of-riders the cold has harmed; so set-off with us to them.
sentences.i: He said: Aslam, I think these are travellers whom the cold has distressed, so come with me to them.
sentences.n: The print writes اضّربهم (here and below, اضّربنا) with a shadda on the ض; it reads as أَضَرَّ بِهِمْ "has harmed them" and is pointed so, the printed mark kept.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْنَا حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ فَإِذَا امْرَأَةٌ تُوقِدُ نَارًا تَحْتَ قِدْرٍ وَمَعَهَا صِبْيَانٌ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajnā ḥattā atayna ilayhim fa-idhā imraʾatun tūqidu nāran taḥta qidrin wa-maʿahā ṣibyānun yatadarraʿūna
sentences.l: And we went out until we came to them, and behold, a woman kindling a fire under a pot, and with her boys crying-imploringly.
sentences.i: We went out until we reached them, and there was a woman lighting a fire under a pot, with boys beside her crying and pleading.
sentences.n: يَتَضَرَّعُونَ is to plead humbly, to cry out in distress; here it is the children's hunger-cries.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عُمَرُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَصْحَابَ الضَّوْءِ وَكَرِهَ أَنْ يَقُولَ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ مَا بَا لَكُمْ قَالَتْ أَضَّرَبِنَا الْبَرْدُ وَاللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿUmaru al-salāmu ʿalaykum aṣḥāba al-ḍawʾi wa-kariha an yaqūla aṣḥāba al-nāri mā bā lakum qālat aḍarra binā al-bardu wa-al-laylu
sentences.l: And ʿUmar said: Peace be upon you, companions of the light! — and he disliked to say “companions of the fire” — What is it with you? She said: The cold and the night have harmed us.
sentences.i: ʿUmar said: Peace be upon you, people of the light! — he disliked saying “people of the fire” — What is the matter with you? She said: The cold and the night have distressed us.
sentences.n: He says أَصْحَابَ الضَّوْءِ because أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ is the Qurʾānic phrase for the people of Hell. The print splits مَا بَالَكُمْ "what is your state?" into مَا بَا لَكُمْ; it is kept as printed. As before, اضّربنا is pointed أَضَرَّ بِنَا, keeping the printed shadda on the ض.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمِ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ قَالَتْ مِنَ الْجُوعِ قَالَ فَمَا هَذِهِ الْقِدْرُ قَالَتْ مَا أُسْكِتُهُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ لَبَسْأَ لَهُ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ بِهِ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-mā bālu hāʾulāʾi al-qawmi yatadarraʿūna qālat mina al-jūʿi qāla fa-mā hādhihi al-qidru qālat mā uskituhum bihi wa-inna ʿUmara ibna al-Khaṭṭābi labasʾa lahu Allāhu ʿanhum yawma al-qiyāmati bihi
sentences.l: He said: And what is the state of these people crying-imploringly? She said: From hunger. He said: And what is this pot? She said: That with which I quiet them; and truly ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — God will ask … him about them on the day of the standing, for it.
sentences.i: He said: And what is the matter with these people, that they cry out? She said: Hunger. He said: And what is this pot? She said: It is what I quiet them with. And as for ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, God will question him about them on the Day of Resurrection because of it.
sentences.n: The pot holds only water (or stones) to keep the children hoping; the woman does not know she is speaking to ʿUmar. The print has لبسأ له, apparently a slip for لَيَسْأَلُهُ "will surely ask him", with ب for ي and a stray space; it is kept as printed and read by the sense.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَمَا يَدْرِي عُمَرُ بِحَالِهِمْ قَالَتْ كَيْفَ يَتَوَلَّى أُمُورَ النَّاسِ وَيَغْفُلُ عَنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-mā yadrī ʿUmaru bi-ḥālihim qālat kayfa yatawallā umūra al-nāsi wa-yaghfulu ʿanhum
sentences.l: He said: And what does ʿUmar know of their condition? She said: How does he take-charge of the affairs of the people and neglect them?
sentences.i: He said: And how would ʿUmar know how they are? She said: How can he take charge of the people's affairs and be heedless of them?

sentences.t: قَالَ أَسْلَمُ فَأَقْبَلَ عُمَرُ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَ انْطَلِقْ بِنَا فَخَرَجْنَا نُهَرْوِلُ حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا دَارَ الصَّرْفِ فَأَخْرَجَ عَدْلًا فِيهِ دَقِيقٌ وَإِنَاءً فِيهِ شَحْمٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ حَمِّلْنِي هَذَا
sentences.tr: qāla Aslamu fa-aqbala ʿUmaru ʿalayya wa-qāla inṭaliq binā fa-kharajnā nuharwilu ḥattā atayna dāra al-ṣarfi fa-akhraja ʿadlan fīhi daqīqun wa-ināʾan fīhi shaḥmun thumma qāla ḥammilnī hādhā
sentences.l: Aslam said: And ʿUmar turned to me and said: Set off with us. So we went out hurrying, until we came to the house of the disbursement, and he brought-out a sack in which was flour, and a vessel in which was fat; then he said: Load me with this.
sentences.i: Aslam said: ʿUmar turned to me and said: Come on. We hurried out until we reached the storehouse, and he took out a sack of flour and a vessel of fat. Then he said: Load this on me.
sentences.n: دَار الصَّرْف is read as a storehouse from which provisions are paid out; the name is odd (صَرْف is also "exchange") and may be a slip for a flour-store. The print has إِنَاءً in the accusative, as if it were governed by أَخْرَجَ ("and a vessel"), which is how it is pointed.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ أَنَا أَحْمِلُهُ عَنْكَ بَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَقَالَ أَتَحْمِلُ عَنِّي وِزْرِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَحَمَّلْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ وَخَرَجْنَا نُهَرْوِلُ حَتَّى أَلْقَيْنَا ذَلِكَ الْعَدْلَ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu anā aḥmiluhu ʿanka bā amīra al-muʾminīna fa-qāla a-taḥmilu ʿannī wizrī yawma al-qiyāmati fa-ḥammaltuhu iyyāhu wa-kharajnā nuharwilu ḥattā alqaynā dhālika al-ʿadla ʿindahā
sentences.l: And I said: I will carry it for you, O commander of the believers. And he said: Will you carry for me my burden on the day of the standing? So I loaded him with it, and we went out hurrying, until we threw down that sack beside her.
sentences.i: I said: I will carry it for you, Commander of the Faithful. He said: Will you carry my burden for me on the Day of Resurrection? So I loaded it on him, and we hurried out until we set that sack down beside her.
sentences.n: The print writes بَا for يَا before أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ, a slip kept as printed. وِزْر is both a load and a burden of sin, which is the pun in ʿUmar's reply: he will bear the weight of the sack himself rather than leave his own sin for the Day of Resurrection.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَ مِنَ الدَّقِيقِ شَيْأً وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ لِلْمَرْأَةِ تَرَدَّدِي إِلَيَّ وَكَانَ يَنْفُخُ تَحْتَ الْقِدْرِ وَكَانَ ذُو لِحْيَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ فَرَأَيْتُ الدُّخَانَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِ لِحْيَتِهِ حَتَّى طَبَخَ وَأَخَذَ مِقْدَارًا مِنَ الشَّحْمِ فَرَمَاهُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhraja mina al-daqīqi shayʾan wa-jaʿala yaqūlu li-al-marʾati taraddadī ilayya wa-kāna yanfukhu taḥta al-qidri wa-kāna dhū liḥyatin ʿaẓīmatin fa-raʾaytu al-dukhāna yakhruju min khilāli liḥyatihi ḥattā ṭabakha wa-akhadha miqdāran mina al-shaḥmi fa-ramāhu fīhi
sentences.l: Then he took out some of the flour, and began to say to the woman: Go-back-and-forth to me. And he was blowing under the pot, and he was one-with-a-great-beard, and I saw the smoke going out from between his beard, until he cooked; and he took an amount of the fat and threw it in it.
sentences.i: Then he took out some of the flour and began saying to the woman: Come back to me for more. He knelt blowing under the pot, a man with a great beard, and I saw the smoke come out through his beard, until the food was cooked; and he took a measure of the fat and threw it in.
sentences.n: وَكَانَ ذُو لِحْيَةٍ is pointed as printed, with ذُو in the nominative where Classical Arabic would have كَانَ ذَا; the text keeps the form. تَرَدَّدِي إِلَيَّ is addressed to the woman, who is to keep coming to him for more flour as she needs it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ أَطْعِمِيهِمْ وَأَنَا أُبَرِّدُ لَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا حَتَّى أَكَلُوا وَشَبِعُوا وَتَرَكَ الْبَاقِيَ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla aṭʿimīhim wa-anā ubarridu lahum wa-lam yazālū ḥattā akalū wa-shabiʿū wa-taraka al-bāqiya ʿindahā
sentences.l: Then he said: Feed them, and I will cool it for them. And they did not cease until they ate and were sated; and he left the remainder with her.
sentences.i: Then he said: Feed them, and I will cool it for them. They kept on until they had eaten and were full, and he left what remained with her.
sentences.n: The print has لَمْ يَزَالُوا with the plural ending kept, though Classical Arabic would drop the final nūn but not the alif of the plural; read by sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَ يَا أَسْلَمُ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ الْجُوعَ أَبْكَاهُمْ فَأَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ لَا أَنْصَرِفَ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لِي سَبَبُ الضَّوْءِ الَّذِي رَأَيْتُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalayya wa-qāla yā Aslamu innī raʾaytu al-jūʿa abkāhum fa-aḥbabtu an lā anṣarifa ḥattā yatabayyana lī sababu al-ḍawʾi alladhī raʾaytuhu
sentences.l: Then he turned to me and said: O Aslam, I saw hunger had made them weep, and I wished not to go away until the cause of the light I saw became clear to me.
sentences.i: Then he turned to me and said: Aslam, I saw that hunger had made them weep, and I did not want to leave until I knew the cause of the light I had seen.
sentences.n: The "light" is the fire that drew them from the road; ʿUmar wanted to learn the cause of the light on the horizon before turning away.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahr Zād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night. The print writes her name as two words and without the alif, شَهْرَ زاد; here it is shahra zāda, kept so.
